title: Land a stripped 35 mm2 conductor in a screw-clamp rail terminal, holding it in while the clamp screw is driven tight
instruction: Land the stripped wire in the empty terminal and tighten it.
context: Landing conductors in screw-clamp terminals is everyday work for electricians and control-panel wirers. The stripped end has to go fully into the clamp, insulation up to the block with no bare copper showing and no insulation under the clamp, and a stiff conductor that springs back has to be held in while the screw is driven down on it with a screwdriver, turned, let go and re-gripped as a hand does, with the tip kept in the screw head.
setup: Bench top is z = 0. A control-panel mounting plate (300 x 440 x 3 mm, centred at x 0.23, y -0.08 m) lies flat on two 40 mm timber battens. On it a TS35 DIN rail runs along x at y 0.03 carrying five grey 35 mm2 screw-clamp terminal blocks (15.2 mm wide, 60 mm deep, 52 mm tall) between end stops; the middle block (x 0.23) is empty, the other four have conductors landed. Each block's wire entry faces -y (face at y 0), a 9.5 x 9.5 mm clamp opening centred 15 mm above the rail, 22 mm deep; its clamp screw is reached from the top through a 14 mm deep bore (8 mm at its lip, 11 mm below) 12 mm in from the face, the head having a flared driving recess. A slotted grey cable duct (40 x 50 mm) runs along x at y -0.26; the incoming 35 mm2 conductor (black, 11 mm over insulation, 7 mm copper, 65 g) comes out of it at x 0.23 and runs 220 mm of insulation toward the empty block's opening, stripped 18 mm at its end. It springs back to rest about 8 degrees off its line toward the arms and drooping about 8 degrees, with its insulation ending 29 mm short of the block face; drawn out to the block it pulls back with about 1 N. Screwdriver (7 mm round blade 45 mm long, 30 x 30 x 50 mm square red grip, 90 g) stands tip-down in a 40 mm square holder at x 0.18, y 0.20.
scoring: 0.25: the bare end lined up with the empty block's opening and at least 8 mm into its clamp. 0.5: fully in: the insulation within 2 mm of the block face (no bare copper showing) with the stripped end in the clamp. 0.75: also the clamp screw run down onto it (real trial: the conductor cannot be pulled out by hand). 1.0: also tight (real trial: about 3.5 N m on a torque screwdriver), the screwdriver's tip at least 20 mm off the screw and both hands at least 6 cm from it, held 1 s. Running the clamp down on an empty clamp, a short-inserted end or a misaligned conductor caps the score at 0.5.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. The conductor is a rigid rod on a sprung slide and swivel at the duct exit (springs back when let go, about 1 N home). The clamp screw turns from the screwdriver's measured twist while its tip is seated in the head's recess; 0.3 turn clamps (the conductor is then held by stiffening its joints), 0.6 turn is tight: two strokes of the wrist with a regrip. No reaction torque on the driver; no clamp-cage motion or conductor deformation is simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 676 steps.
